Congruence vs Similarity

Congruent triangles have exactly the same area. In contrast, similar triangles only have the same shape, and the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Conditions for Congruence

Two triangles are strictly congruent if they satisfy any of the five standard criteria: SSS (Side-Side-Side), SAS (Side-Angle-Side), ASA (Angle-Side-Angle), AAS (Angle-Angle-Side), or RHS (Right angle-Hypotenuse-Side).

Area of a Triangle

The general formula for the area of a triangle is Area = 1/2 × base × height. Since congruent triangles possess equal corresponding bases and equal corresponding altitudes, their areas are naturally identical.

questions.question: In a ∆PQR, PQ = PR and PT is perpendicular to QR. If PQ = 17 cm, PT = 15 cm, then what is the measure (in cm) of QR?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In an isosceles triangle, the altitude drawn to the unequal side bisects the base.

This splits the triangle into two identical right-angled triangles.

Using the standard Pythagorean triplet (8, 15, 17), if the hypotenuse = 17 and perpendicular = 15, then the base (QT) = 8.

Since the altitude bisects the base, the total length of QR is twice the length of QT.

⇒ QR = 2 × 8 = 16 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ In ΔPQR, PQ = PR = 17 cm.

⇒ PT ⊥ QR and PT = 15 cm.

 
 
• 
 P Q R T 17 cm 17 cm 15 cm x x 

**Concept Used:**

⇒ The altitude drawn from the vertex of an isosceles triangle to its base exactly bisects the base.

⇒ ∴ QT = TR = QR ÷ 2.

**Calculation:**

⇒ In right-angled ΔPQT, apply Pythagoras theorem:

⇒ PQ² = PT² + QT²

⇒ 17² = 15² + QT²

⇒ 289 = 225 + QT²

⇒ QT² = 289 − 225 = 64

⇒ QT = √64 = 8 cm.

⇒ Since QT is exactly half of the base QR:

⇒ QR = 2 × QT

⇒ QR = 2 × 8 = 16 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Isosceles Triangles

In an isosceles triangle, the two angles opposite to the equal sides are also equal. Furthermore, the altitude drawn to the unequal side functions as an angle bisector and median simultaneously.

Pythagoras Theorem

Applicable only to right-angled triangles, it dictates that the square of the longest side (hypotenuse) equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides: a² + b² = c².

Common Pythagorean Triplets

Memorising frequent integer combinations dramatically reduces exam calculation time. Core examples include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), (7, 24, 25), and (9, 40, 41).

questions.question: The perimeter of an isosceles triangle is 80 cm. If the side that is not equal in length to any of the other two sides is 20 cm, find the length of each of the equal sides.
questions.solution:

length of an unequal side = 20 cm.

P = 2a + b units. Where P = Perimeter, a = length of two equal sides. and b = length of base or unequal side.

**CALCULATION:**

Here P = 80 cm , b = 20 cm 

⇒P = 2a + b 

⇒ 80 = 2a + 20 

⇒2a = 60

questions.question: If a 7-storey building has a 28 m long shadow, the number of storeys of the building whose shadow is 48 m long is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **shadow problems**, the height and shadow length are in **direct proportion**.

Ratio (Height : Shadow) → 7 : 28 ⇒ 1 : 4

This means every 1 storey creates a 4 m shadow.

For a 48 m shadow, number of **storeys** = 48 ÷ 4 = 12.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 storeys.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of storeys of first building (H₁) = 7

Shadow length of first building (S₁) = 28 m

Shadow length of second building (S₂) = 48 m

**Formula Used:**

For objects at the same time and place, (Height₁ / Shadow₁) = (Height₂ / Shadow₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/99b5b8fdc910a15fd871bd19f683edb5299965950dde7ab0973c551d310c362e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the number of storeys of the second building be **x**.

⇒ 7 / 28 = x / 48

⇒ 1 / 4 = x / 48

⇒ x = 48 ÷ 4

⇒ x = 12

Therefore, the building has 12 storeys, which corresponds to **option (4)**.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 storeys.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Proportion

Two quantities are in direct proportion if the ratio of their values remains constant (x/y = k). Here, Height ∝ Shadow length.

Similar Triangles in Shadows

Shadow problems are geometric applications of **similar triangles**, where the sun's rays are parallel, making the ratio of Height to Base (Shadow) identical for all vertical objects.

Unitary Method

A technique where you find the value of a **single unit** (e.g., length of shadow per storey) and then multiply to find the required value.</p

questions.question: If ∆ABC and ∆QPR are congruent triangles such that AB = 7 cm, AC = 8 cm, ∠B = 65° and ∠C = 75°, then which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For congruent triangles ΔABC ≅ ΔQPR, the vertices map to each other in the exact order written.

Mappings: A → Q, B → P, C → R.

Side PQ maps directly to AB, so PQ = AB = 7 cm.

Angle R maps directly to angle C, so ∠R = ∠C = 75°.

This matches the given condition perfectly without calculating any other unknown sides or angles.

**∴ The correct answer is PQ = 7 cm and ∠R = 75°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ ΔABC ≅ ΔQPR

⇒ AB = 7 cm, AC = 8 cm

⇒ ∠B = 65°, ∠C = 75°

**Concept Used:**

⇒ CPCT (Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles): If two triangles are congruent, their corresponding angles and sides are precisely equal.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since ΔABC ≅ ΔQPR, the exact correspondence is given by A ↔ Q, B ↔ P, and C ↔ R.

⇒ Corresponding sides match: AB = QP, BC = PR, and AC = QR

⇒ Corresponding angles match: ∠A = ∠Q, ∠B = ∠P, and ∠C = ∠R

⇒ Applying the given dimensions directly to the mapped parts:

⇒ PQ = AB = 7 cm

⇒ QR = AC = 8 cm

⇒ ∠P = ∠B = 65°

⇒ ∠R = ∠C = 75°

⇒ Also, by the angle sum property, ∠A = 180° − (65° + 75°) = 40°, meaning ∠Q = 40°.

⇒ Comparing our derived values with the given options, we find that PQ = 7 cm and ∠R = 75° is the only correct statement.

**∴ The correct answer is PQ = 7 cm and ∠R = 75°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Congruence Criteria

Two triangles are strictly congruent if they satisfy SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, or RHS congruency conditions.

CPCT Theorem

CPCT denotes 'Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles'. It establishes that if two triangles are congruent, all their equivalent angles and sides are identical.

Angle Sum Property

The total sum of interior angles in any triangle is exactly 180°. This helps determine the third angle if two are known (∠A = 180° − ∠B − ∠C).

Similar vs Congruent

Congruent triangles have an identical shape and exact size, whereas similar triangles possess the identical shape but may differ proportionally in size.

questions.question: In ΔABC, P and Q are the middle points of the sides AB and AC, respectively. R is a point on the segment PQ such that PR : RQ = 1 : 5. If PR = 6 cm, then BC = _______.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

In ΔABC, P and Q are the middle points of the sides AB and AC, respectively. R is a point on the segment PQ such that PR : RQ = 1 : 5. PR = 6 cm.

**Formula Used:**

In a triangle, the line segment joining the midpoints of two sides is parallel to the third side and half of it (Midpoint Theorem).

**Calculation:**

According to the Midpoint Theorem, PQ is parallel to BC and PQ = ½ BC.

Given PR : RQ = 1 : 5, so PR / RQ = 1 / 5.

Let RQ = x.

Then, PR = 6 cm and PR / RQ = 6 / x = 1 / 5.

⇒ 6 / x = 1 / 5

⇒ 6 = x / 5

⇒ x = 30 cm

Thus, PQ = PR + RQ = 6 + 30 = 36 cm.

Since PQ = ½ BC, we have:

⇒ BC = 2 × PQ

⇒ BC = 2 × 36

⇒ BC = 72 cm

**The length of BC is 72 cm.**

questions.question: In a triangle LMN, ∠L = 118° and LM = LN. Find ∠N.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Since LM = LN, ΔLMN is an isosceles triangle.

Angles opposite to equal sides are equal, meaning ∠M = ∠N.

Using the angle sum property of a triangle: ∠L + 2 × ∠N = 180°

118° + 2 × ∠N = 180° ⇒ 2 × ∠N = 62°

∠N = 62° ÷ 2 = 31°

**∴ The correct answer is 31°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

∠L = 118°

LM = LN

**Formula Used:**

The sum of interior angles of a triangle is 180°.

Angles opposite to equal sides of an isosceles triangle are equal.

**Calculations:**

⇒ In ΔLMN, LM = LN

⇒ ∴ ∠M = ∠N (Angles opposite to equal sides)

⇒ ∠L + ∠M + ∠N = 180°

⇒ 118° + ∠N + ∠N = 180°

⇒ 2 × ∠N = 180° − 118°

⇒ 2 × ∠N = 62°

⇒ ∠N = 62° ÷ 2 = 31°

**∴ The correct answer is 31°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Isosceles Triangle Property

A triangle in which any two sides are equal is an isosceles triangle. The angles opposite to the equal sides are always equal.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all three interior angles of a triangle is strictly equal to 180°.

Exterior Angle Property

The exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles.

Congruence of Triangles

Two triangles are strictly congruent if they share the exact same shape and size. The primary criteria for congruence are SSS (Side-Side-Side), SAS (Side-Angle-Side), ASA (Angle-Side-Angle), AAS (Angle-Angle-Side), and RHS (Right angle-Hypotenuse-Side).

questions.question: Let ABC be a triangle. If the mid-points of AB, BC and AC are D, E and F, respectively, then △DEF is NOT congruent to ____.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

According to the Midpoint Theorem, joining the midpoints of all three sides of a triangle divides it into four identical (congruent) smaller triangles.

The four resulting triangles are △ADF, △BDE, △ECF, and △DEF.

Therefore, △DEF is exactly congruent in shape and size to △ADF, △BDE, and △ECF.

However, the parent triangle △ABC is four times larger in area compared to △DEF, meaning they are similar, but NOT congruent.

**∴ The correct answer is △ABC.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formula Used:**

**Midpoint Theorem:** The line segment joining the midpoints of any two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and equal to half of its length.

**Calculations:**

⇒ By Midpoint Theorem, DE ∥ AC and DE = ¹÷₂ × AC = AF = FC

⇒ EF ∥ AB and EF = ¹÷₂ × AB = AD = DB

⇒ DF ∥ BC and DF = ¹÷₂ × BC = BE = EC

⇒ Now, let's compare △DEF and △BDE:

⇒ DE = DE (Common side)

⇒ EF = BD (Since EF is half of AB)

⇒ DF = BE (Since DF is half of BC)

⇒ By SSS (Side-Side-Side) congruence criterion, △DEF ≅ △BDE.

⇒ Similarly, by comparing the sides, we can establish that △DEF ≅ △ECF and △DEF ≅ △ADF.

⇒ Since △ABC is the main enclosing triangle, its side lengths are precisely double the sides of △DEF, which makes them similar but significantly different in overall size.

⇒ Hence, △DEF is NOT congruent to △ABC.

**∴ The correct answer is △ABC.**

questions.question: If Δ ABC~Δ FDE such that AB = 9 cm, AC = 11 cm, DF = 16 cm and DE = 12 cm, then the length of BC is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two triangles are **similar** (ΔABC ~ ΔFDE), their **corresponding sides** are proportional.

The ratio is: AB / FD = BC / DE = AC / FE

⇒ 9 / 16 = BC / 12

⇒ BC = (9 × 12) ÷ 16

⇒ BC = 108 ÷ 16 = 27 ÷ 4 = 6(3)/(4) cm

**∴ The correct answer is 6(3)/(4) cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** AB = 9 cm, AC = 11 cm, DF = 16 cm, and DE = 12 cm. It is given that **Δ ABC ~ Δ FDE**.

**Formula Used:** If two triangles are similar, the **ratio** of their corresponding sides is **constant**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a5674dc185710760be6f43d58a6d33bd987c50d170fd388de9c5bfb4917b9843.png] 

Since **Δ ABC ~ Δ FDE**, we match the corresponding vertices:

A ↔ F, B ↔ D, and C ↔ E.

⇒ AB ÷ FD = BC ÷ DE

⇒ 9 ÷ 16 = BC ÷ 12

⇒ 16 × BC = 9 × 12

⇒ 16 × BC = 108

⇒ BC = 108 ÷ 16

⇒ BC = 27 ÷ 4

⇒ BC = 6.75 cm = 6(3)/(4) cm

**∴ The correct answer is 6(3)/(4) cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Similar Triangles

Two triangles are similar if their corresponding angles are equal and their **corresponding sides** are in the same **ratio**.

Ratio of **Perimeters** = Ratio of **Corresponding Sides**; Ratio of **Areas** = (Ratio of Corresponding Sides)².

SAS Similarity Criteria

If one angle of a triangle is equal to one angle of another triangle and the sides including these angles are **proportional**, then the triangles are similar.</p

⇒ 3rd angle = 3x

⇒ 3rd angle = 3x = 3 times 30 = 90°

questions.question: The side BC of triangle ABC is produced to a point D. If AC = BC and ∠BAC = 70º, then find the value of ∠ACD - ∠ ABC .
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the Exterior Angle Theorem, an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles.

⇒ ∠ACD = ∠BAC + ∠ABC

Rearranging the terms, we directly get:

⇒ ∠ACD − ∠ABC = ∠BAC

Given ∠BAC = 70°, the result is 70°.

**∴ The correct answer is 70°.**
